body:
### UTC Date & Time

[June 25, 2026, 14:00 UTC](https://savvytime.com/converter/utc/jun-25-2026/2pm)

### Agenda

Devnet updates:
- Glamsterdam Devnet-5: What's the current status and are client teams getting support? 
- Devnet-6 readiness status?
- Test slashing validators pre-fork — Nico Flaig raised on ACDT #84: we should test EIP-8045 (exclude slashed validators) properly before mainnet. Is this planned?
- Spec bug? [https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/issues/5399]

Other topics:
- Builder API — remove `submitBeaconBlock` (builder-specs#162). Revisit now that devnet-6 is about to launch with builder integration. (bharath-123)
- Builder API — circuit breakers — `@bharath-123`: should we specify clients MUST fallback to self-build with impl-dependent heuristics (like Bellatrix)? Standardize or leave flexible?
- FYI Staked Builder API (builder-specs#138) has been merged. 
- Proposer Preferences API — remaining concerns on beacon-APIs#608? (james-prysm)
- Has anyone reviewed this? Beacon API #618 validator state renaming — breaking change; `pending-queued` states outdated post-EIP-6110/7251. Ecosystem tooling impact assessed? (leobago, barnabasbusa)
-  (feat: extend /eth/v1/node/peers with peer scoring and disconnect reasons)[Beacon API #606] — requested by `@barnabasbusa`. Status?


Glamsterdam:
- EIP-8080 DFI — let exits use consolidation queue. Intent to DFI stated in PQ Interop #15. Any remaining blockers?
- EIP-8045 SFI — exclude slashed validators from proposing. Was CFI→SFI in #179. Potuz to open Prysm PR — status? Can we SFI now?
- EIP-8282 — builder execution requests. `@nflaig` requested discussion at #180. DoS attack surface vs. impl cost tradeoff assessed? Builder deposit limit risk revisited?

Hegota:

- Hegota non-headliner window — opened after EL headliner decision. End date still TBD based on Glamsterdam progress.

From https://forkcast.org/calls/acdt/084

> No ACDT decision on [EIP-7688](https://forkcast.org/eips/7688) for devnet-7; revisit at ACDC after seeing devnet-6 stability and CL-breakout feedback

Current status:

- [Specs](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4630) (alpha.11)
- [Tests](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4630#issuecomment-4352744403) (alpha.11)
- [Kurtosis](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4630#issuecomment-4377125436) (Nimbus Lodestar Lighthouse)

Rocketpool statement:

> Hey Etan, sorry we aren't able to make the ACD call in person due to the time differences. But feel free to pass on our endorsement of the forward-compatible containers in our absence.
>
> Rocket Pool has recently introduced beacon state proofs to become a more permisionless protocol. With each passing Ethereum hard fork, we must now be conscious that the introduction of new container fields may impact the proof verification logic implemented in our smart contracts. Our contract upgrades go through rigorous testing and security audits and we must have these upgrades deployed ahead of any verification-breaking hard fork Ethereum delivers.
>
> Forward-compatible containers specified in EIP-7688 would reduce the impact of hard forks on our protocol by reducing the likelihood that future state changes force us to undertake a time- and security-sensitive upgrades. The same would hold true for other protocols making use of beacon state proofs.
>
> Glamsterdam is already introducing a breaking change for us with ePBS which we will need to upgrade our proof verification logic to support. For Rocket Pool, the inclusion of EIP-7688 would be well timed as it would allow us to upgrade our verifier a single time to support both changes.

The same arguments and concerns apply to the Lido protocol. Since Dencun, the hard fork that introduced EIP-4788, Lido has gradually transitioned most trusted components that rely on Beacon Chain data to permissionless verification using EIP-4788 proofs. This has enabled Lido to support a truly permissionless staking module, CSM, where both operator onboarding and exit are fully permissionless.

However, because the Beacon Chain state proof formats used with EIP-4788 may change across Ethereum hard forks, the permissionless exit mechanism remains dependent on timely upgrades to the Lido protocol. As a Lido contributor, I would strongly prefer to eliminate this dependency. EIP-7688 appears to largely do so. For that reason, I see significant value in including this EIP in the Glamsterdam hard fork.

**Mascot needed for Glamsterdam upgrade**
🐜🦫🐝🦩🐹🐙🐻‍❄️🐩
Vote for your favorite on Eth Magicians.  **Voting closes July 8**

Top 3 currently: 🦩 38%, 🐻‍❄️ 27% & 🦫 20%

https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/mascot-needed-for-glamsterdam-upgrade/26008

[EIP-8066: Upgrade Mascots](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8066) specifies mascot requirements, role of Mascot Wrestler (@eviljordan) & veto powers of the Mascot Wrestler & client teams.

Announcement:

**Shutter and the "Encrypt The Mempool!" coalition is offering a 3 ETH bounty for feedback on EIPs [8105](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8105) and [8184](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8184).**

Suggested topics include:

- dealing with key withholding attacks
- leveraging FRAME transactions
- improving transaction execution quality
- and more!

If you have feedback, please share your feedback and submit a claim by EOD July 30.
If you just want to Encrypt The Mempool, please add funds (even 0.001 ETH) to the bounty pool.

https://poidh.xyz/mainnet/bounty/11

Announcement:

**The "Encrypt The Mempool!" coalition is seeking a Consensus Client developer or team to develop the [8184](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8184) consensus spec.**

For more info, see: https://github.com/jflo/lucid-pm

Please contact me or Justin (Besu) if interested.
